name: Renfield Shake Motor
description:
12V shake motor - 'the signature', Renfield's tremble. Cytron MDD (MDD10A-class, DIR+PWM per channel) on channel 1. BCM GPIO: DIR1=26, PWM1=13.

This MATCHES fleet convention - GPIO 13 is the PWM line on every MDD10A in MonsterBox, and PumpkinHead uses the identical pair (DIR=26, PWM=13). The pins were briefly wired the other way round on 2026-09-13 and the operator swapped them back the same day; if you find a note anywhere claiming Renfield is reversed, it is stale. DIR and PWM are still not interchangeable: swapped, motor_control.py puts the 2kHz PWM train on the DIR line and a static level on the PWM line, so the board sees a permanently-asserted enable with direction chattering - the motor runs flat out and speed does nothing.

TWO-PIN BOARD - do not re-add rpwmPin/lpwmPin/renPin/lenPin. This part was specced for a BTS7960 and never built; the driver changed at the bench. services/hardwareService/index.js dispatches on controlBoard === 'BTS7960' && rpwmPin != null && lpwmPin != null, and killInFlightDrive() tests rpwmPin BEFORE directionPin - so stale four-pin keys send both the drive and the stop down the BTS7960 path, against pins this board does not have, while still reporting success.

POWER: 12V PSU -> slow-blow fuse -> NTC inrush limiter (5-10 ohm) -> B+. 10,000uF/25V+ across B+/B- at the board, stripe to B-; without the NTC that cap is a dead short at power-on and trips the PSU's OCP. RC snubber (0.1uF film + 10-47 ohm 1W) across the MOTOR terminals at the motor - a bare cap with no series resistor shorts the H-bridge on every PWM edge and cooks the MOSFETs. Star ground at B-; Pi GND runs to the control header GND only, carrying signal return, never motor current. The 12V motor supply must NOT share the Pi's 5V rail.

PULL-DOWNS: 10k from DIR and PWM to GND at the driver end. scripts/motor_control.py calls gpio_free() on both pins when a run ends and a Pi reboot returns them to input, so both float otherwise - on a yard prop that reads as the motor running when nobody is home.

STALL: a wiper-class motor stalls at roughly 24-40A, above the MDD10A's 30A peak. Short bursts only - scenes run 900-2000ms at 50-80% and maxDuration caps any single energization at 5000ms. Groundbreaker's wiper motor stalled mid-test 2026-08-30 and its 12V rail is still dead; a stalled motor cooks until the fuse opens, and PWM outlives the process.
